# ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry Daily Update (Aug 20, 2026)
## OVERVIEW 
The day saw significant progress in the Lokahi interop development, particularly in defining storage mechanisms, refining message validity rules, and advancing multi-chain L1 watcher capabilities. Discussions also clarified the removal of the cross-unsafe chain-head notion from Go.

## KEY TECHNICAL DEVELOPMENTS

### Lokahi Interop Storage and Verification Round Loop
The Lokahi interop development focused on establishing robust storage solutions, including a verified store, per-chain log stores, and an invalidated-output archive. This work also laid the groundwork for the verification round loop, which observes chains and L1, makes decisions, and applies them. Key decisions were made regarding checksum computation placement and the handling of `Invalidate` and `Rewind` decisions.
- Verified store, log store, and invalidated-output archive implemented in `lokahi-interop` [#22535](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/22535).
- Verification round loop implemented, including cold start and handling of `Invalidate`/`Rewind` decisions [#22536](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/22536).
- Clarification on the archive write mechanism to ensure idempotence and prevent data loss during crash-replay scenarios [#22540](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/22540).

### Multi-Chain L1 Watcher and Service Composition
Efforts continued to generalize the L1 watcher to handle multiple chains and to compose multi-chain services within Lokahi. This involved significant refactoring to accommodate multiple chains efficiently and to ensure proper configuration and data handling.
- Multi-chain L1 watcher implementation, addressing `tokio::select!` refactoring challenges and per-chain query channels [#22531](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/22531).
- N-chain service composition and configuration, including layered config, per-chain data directories, and RPC/metric registration [#22532](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/22532).

### Interop Message Validity Rules and Metrics
Consolidation of interop message validity rules into a single source was a key focus, ensuring consistent application across the Lokahi verifier and the proof side. Additionally, discussions around adding `chain_id` labels to Kona's metrics aimed to improve observability.
- Consolidation of shared interop message validity rules into `kona-interop`, with discussions on checksum computation and API shape [#22534](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/22534).
- Implementation of `chain_id` metric labels for Kona, addressing macro limitations and testing challenges [#22529](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/22529).

### Removal of Cross-Unsafe Chain-Head Notion
The vestigial cross-unsafe chain-head notion was removed from Go components, streamlining the interop design by eliminating a concept no longer relevant to the current interop architecture.
- Removal of the cross-unsafe chain-head notion from Go components, clarifying its distinction from message-level cross-unsafe validation [#22550](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/22550).

## NEWLY OPENED PULL REQUESTS
- [#1311](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/pull/1311) sepolia-devnet-3: add chain config
- [#1310](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/pull/1310) chore: automated codegen update 2026-08-20

## CLOSED ISSUES
- **Go Cross-Unsafe Chain-Head Removal**: The issue of removing the vestigial cross-unsafe chain-head notion from Go components (op-node, op-service, op-devstack) was closed. This change clarifies that the concept of a distinct cross-unsafe head is no longer relevant to the current interop design, while preserving the message-level cross-unsafe validation. [#22550](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/22550)

## NEW ISSUES
No new issues were opened today.

## ACTIVE ISSUES

### Kona Engine: Targeted Reset
Discussion on [#22526](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/22526) focused on the implementation of a targeted reset mechanism for the Kona engine. The latest comment clarifies that resets should never move the cross-safe head forward, but can move it backward. It highlights a structural difference between `op-node` and `kona` in handling cross-safe head rewinds, with `kona` requiring explicit maintenance of the invariant. The bound for cross-safe head movement is placed in the state transition rather than the reset itself. A deliberate difference in retry ceiling between `reset` and `reset_to` was also noted, with `reset_to` having a bounded number of retries due to fixed heads.

### Kona Engine: Local/Cross-Safe Vocabulary and Promotion Entry Point
The discussion on [#22525](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/22525) centered on renaming head vocabulary to explicit local-safe/cross-safe and establishing a single promotion entry point for cross-safe. The latest comment details the implementation, noting that the "exactly one promoter per engine" property is enforced at the crate boundary. It also highlights two heads that needed re-pointing in opposite directions: the depth-1 lockstep confirmation to the derivation actor must carry *local*-safe, while `FinalizeTask`'s sanity check moved to *cross*-safe. A pre-existing `cargo test` vs `cargo nextest` disagreement on the crate was also noted.

### Kona: Chain_ID Metric Label
On [#22529](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/22529), the discussion revolved around adding a `chain_id` label dimension to Kona's existing metric names. The latest comment details the implementation challenges, particularly with macro limitations that required a new call style for `set!` and `record!`. It also addresses a pre-existing unit test failure related to `PrometheusBuilder::install_recorder()` and clarifies the scope of the implementation to `kona-engine` only. Design decisions, such as placing `chain_id: u64` on `EngineState`, were also discussed.

### Lokahi: Interop Actor, Cross-Safe Happy Path (Phase 3)
The discussion on [#22522](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/22522) provided an index of phase-3 decisions from a Slack design discussion. These decisions cover retention and storage engine, WAL-replay hazard for the invalidated-output archive, and Kona/op-supernode activation-source divergence, indicating ongoing architectural considerations for the Lokahi interop actor.

### Lokahi: Multi-Chain L1 Watcher
Discussion on [#22531](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/22531) focused on generalizing `L1WatcherActor` to handle multiple chains. The latest comment details the implementation, noting that `tokio::select!` shaped the refactor more than the fan-out itself, leading to a design where updates are classified into `L1WatcherEvent` before handling. It also clarifies that `eth_getLogs` remains per-chain, per-chain query channels stay individually fatal, and chain labels are intentionally omitted from the watcher's log lines for now. The chain set is fixed at construction, with an empty set resulting in a panic.

### Lokahi: N-Chain Service Composition and Config
On [#22532](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/22532), the discussion centered on growing `rust/lokahi` for N-chain service composition and configuration. The latest comment details the landing of the PR, which enables `lokahi node --config <file>` to run N chains in one process. It highlights how the L1 head watch, watcher attachment, and engine's chain ID were reconciled during the merge of parallel branch lines. A latent test bug exposed by the merge was also addressed. A decision from @ajsutton confirmed that the L1 watcher's fixed, non-empty chain set is correct by design.

### Kona-Interop: Consolidate Shared Message-Validity Rules
The discussion on [#22534](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/22534) focused on making `kona-interop` the single home for interop message-validity rules. The latest comments clarify that checksum computation is not a consensus-protocol check and belongs in Lokahi's store layer, not in the shared validity rules. It was also decided that the shared interop rules surface should be a type, `MessageRules`, rather than free functions, to improve code organization and discoverability. An enumeration of pre-existing implementations of the five rules was provided, highlighting Rust↔Go divergences for future consideration.

### Lokahi-Interop: Stores (VerifiedDB + WAL, LogsDBs, Invalidated-Output Archive)
On [#22535](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/22535), the discussion revolved around the interop actor's persistent state. The latest comments detail the landing of the PR, which includes the `lokahi-interop` crate with all three stores: verified store, log store, and invalidated-output archive. Key decisions included placing checksum computation in `lokahi-interop` for now, using two different chain-id types, and binary rather than JSON encoding. Earlier discussions established that superroots must be returnable over the full fault dispute window, leading to the decision to use RocksDB for stores and to not prune initially.

### Lokahi-Interop: Verification Round Loop
The discussion on [#22536](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/22536) focused on the lockstep verification round loop. The latest comment details the landing of the PR, which now holds the verification round loop in `lokahi-interop`. Decisions included `Invalidate` and `Rewind` not writing to the WAL, `step` returning a pace instead of sleeping, and carrying through the four verdicts of `local_safe_snapshot_at`.
